preamble: Insertion of the alveolar approximant [ɹ] to break vowel hiatus. In non-rhotic English accents (RP, Boston and others) historical coda r was lost, so word-final r is pronounced only before a vowel (linking r); speakers then extended the [ɹ] to words that never had an r, after a non-high vowel before a vowel (intrusive r): law and order, idea of, drawing.

examples.note: No r in the spelling or etymology; [ɹ] is inserted after a non-high final vowel before a vowel
Word-internal intrusive [ɹ] at a morpheme boundary

languageExamples.context: After a non-high vowel before a vowel, across word and morpheme boundaries
